items.title: India's CERT-In reportedly gets access to restricted Claude Mythos model
items.what: Indian outlets, citing government sources, report that India's cybersecurity agency CERT-In has gained access to Anthropic's restricted model Claude Mythos. The stated aim is to test its ability to detect and potentially exploit system vulnerabilities.
items.why: Models able to find and exploit software flaws can strengthen defence, but wider access to them also increases the chance that the capability leaks or is misused.
items.us: The reports describe the US as having approved sharing the model, which points to the US treating such models as strategic assets.
items.watch: What access terms and safeguards apply, and whether other governments seek similar access.

items.title: CNAS report examines risks of AI in nuclear weapons operations
items.what: The US think tank CNAS published a report on reducing the risks of bringing AI into nuclear weapons operations.
items.why: Errors, false warnings or over-reliance on AI in nuclear command and control could raise the chance of a mistaken or escalating nuclear decision.
items.who: Center for a New American Security (researchers)
items.us: The report is aimed largely at US decision-makers who are weighing AI use in defence.
items.watch: Whether nuclear-armed states adopt or discuss the proposed safeguards.

items.title: China reportedly preparing broad AI safety and ethics standards
items.what: Outlets in the US and Mexico report that China plans to create broad safety and ethics standards for AI development. A World Internet Conference report on frontier AI security and governance was also presented in China.
items.why: Safety rules in a leading AI country could reduce risky development, or could fall short if they are weak or not enforced.
items.who: Chinese authorities, as reported by media
items.us: Chinese standards could shape whether US-China talks on AI risk find common ground.
items.watch: Whether published standards cover frontier-model testing for dangerous capabilities.

items.title: Tencent releases AI model trained with limited cybersecurity data
items.what: Reuters reports that Tencent rolled out an AI model trained with limited cybersecurity data amid fears about hacking.
items.why: Limiting what a model learns about hacking is one way to reduce its usefulness to attackers. Whether such limits hold up matters for the spread of offensive cyber ability.
items.who: Tencent, as reported by Reuters and others
items.watch: Whether independent tests show the model's hacking abilities are actually reduced.

items.title: Altman and Hinton speak on limits and risks of advanced AI
items.what: OpenAI's Sam Altman said human control must set limits on superintelligence. Geoffrey Hinton told The Guardian that the world might turn out to have been better off without AI.
items.why: Leading figures stress that keeping control of very capable AI is unsolved. Experts disagree on how close or how likely such risks are.
items.watch: Whether such statements are followed by concrete commitments or rules.
